dendritic cells from Peyer's patches (PP) are able to promote the production of IgA by B cells, and that this function depends on the presence of intestinal bacteria and is partly mediated by the production of retinoic acid.
intestinal bacteria condition DC to promote IgA responses.
intestinal commensal microbes condition dendritic cells to express a unique phenotype that promotes IgA production.

understanding the role of the immune system in regulating mucosal homeostasis.
the role of intestinal bacteria and their metabolites in regulating immune responses in the intestinal mucosa.
the role of dendritic cells in the regulation of IgA production.

intestinal bacteria are able to condition dendritic cells to promote IgA-producing B cells.
intestinal commensal bacterial products, including LPS, condition PP-DC to express BAFF, APRIL, iNOS and VIP receptors.
the intestinal commensal microbiota is responsible for the unique ability of PP-derived DC to instruct naïve intestinal B cells to differentiate to IgA producing plasma blasts.

the presence of commensal bacteria on intestinal epithelium is crucial for the development of a mucosal immune system capable of producing high levels of secreted IgA, the predominant antibody isotypes at the intestinal mucosal.
